name: Chablis

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Chardonnay sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Bourgogne, village, Premier Cru, Grand Cru
Burgundy's four levels, from regional Bourgogne up through village wines to Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards.
keyfacts: Chablis has four levels: Petit Chablis, Chablis, Premier Cru and Grand Cru, with Chablis AOC designated in 1938 and Petit Chablis in 1944.
Chablis, Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards lie mainly on Kimmeridgian soils, while Petit Chablis is mainly grown on Portlandian soils on the higher slopes and plateau.
The seven Grand Cru vineyards lie on one southwest-facing hill next to the town: Bougros, Preuses, Vaudésir, Grenouilles, Valmur, Les Clos and Blanchot.
Spring frost is a major risk, and growers protect vines with heaters, candles and water sprays that coat the buds in ice.

notes: Chablis's cool climate gives Chardonnay more acidity and less fruit than warmer regions do.
Racy, green-apple acidity is its trademark, and the style is crisper and steelier than the rest of Burgundy.
Chablis was traditionally aged in old, neutral barrels that added no oak flavor.
Some Chablis has an earthy, wet stone flavor that grows with age before mellowing into delicate honeyed notes.
Grand cru Chablis can often age well over 15 years, and many premiers crus at least 10.

blurb.text: A Burgundy appellation in the far north of the region, making dry white wine from Chardonnay alone. The cool climate gives high acidity and less fruitiness, often with a flinty or steely note, and oak influence is usually much lighter than elsewhere in Burgundy.
